records.region: California/Nevada Death Valley region: Copper Canyon–Last Chance Canyon, Death Valley Wash, Mesquite Flat, Salt Creek, Cottonball Basin and Middle Basin
records.candidate_name_role: Distinct, bounded local-reach candidates only; no completed whole-system representative identity.
records.material_pending_reason: Readable source maps cover the full selected geographic footprint but do not establish the western canyon/fan-to-Death Valley Wash connection or the long selected transfer from Death Valley Wash across Mesquite Flat into Salt Creek. These are substantive selected through-link gaps, rather than an access failure or a completed name-scope hold.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual endpoint is within Middle Basin on the mapped Salt Creek corridor, south of the Furnace Creek Wash receiving setting. Cottonball Marsh lies on the separate western side of Cottonball Basin. The selected upper opening is in the Copper Canyon–Last Chance Canyon setting, not the distinct northeastern Cottonwood Creek/Oriental Wash approach. No Amargosa River identity is transferred from the wider Death Valley basin.
records.completion_scope: All 50 selected parts, opening, material joins, basin passages and actual Middle Basin tip were considered using readable maps of the full geographic footprint. Whole-route correspondence is withheld for two specific through-link gaps; exact banks, current flow and geometry repair were not required.
records.supported_name_scope: Direct source labels support the two local watercourse names. Copper Canyon, Last Chance Canyon, Mesquite Flat, Cottonball Basin and Middle Basin are landform or basin labels, not interchangeable river names.

scope_limits: The maps establish the upper canyon setting but not the full western fan passage into Death Valley Wash.
The selected long Mesquite Flat passage is not established by a mapped through-channel or independent source account connecting the two named reaches.
Distinct names on confirmed local reaches do not by themselves disprove a representative system identity; the decisive obstacle here is incomplete selected through-link correspondence.
Basin shading and drainage symbols are not proof of current water, continuous surface flow, present wetland extent or precise channel banks.
The actual modeled terminal is not asserted to be the natural end of Salt Creek; the source depicts the drainage continuing beyond it.

bounded_name_observations.name: Death Valley Wash
bounded_name_observations.scope: Named northern/middle wash corridor only; western fan and Mesquite Flat transfer remain unresolved.

bounded_name_observations.name: Salt Creek
bounded_name_observations.scope: Named southeastern corridor through Cottonball Basin to the selected Middle Basin tip; not assigned to the entire modeled group.

records.region: Western side of Lago de Maracaibo, Zulia; Sierra de Perijá–Palmar corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: This is the western Maracaibo Río Palmar descending from Sierra de Perijá. The eastern same-named river draining toward Los Olivitos is separately depicted in the Zulia hydrography and is not this selected system.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded ordinary-corridor source correspondence for the single selected fragment, all 35 parts, chosen upper Palmar opening, principal join/impoundment passage, intermediate reaches, lake approach and actual terminal. The sources support Río Palmar as representative identity without a material unviewed through-link.
records.supported_name_scope: The selected upper Palmar, impoundment/junction corridor, middle and lower river to Lago de Maracaibo. This is a representative identity, not a scalar assignment to every tributary or reservoir.

scope_limits: The name is a source-supported representative identity. Formal registry status and one scalar name for every stored vertex are unverified.
Published length statements differ in scope from the retained 144.307 km model measurement and are not used to redefine the target.
The earliest selected short headwater position is matched at ordinary corridor scale; an exact spring, bank, confluence vertex or contemporary shoreline is outside this finding.
The sources account for El Diluvio/Tres Ríos geographically. No current engineering or operational condition is inferred.

records.region: Antofagasta Region, northern Chile; inland channels east of Antofagasta, with the Salar Mar Muerto passage.
records.candidate_name_role: No whole selected-system natural-river identity established. Salar Mar Muerto is a mapped intervening salt-flat component; Chimborazo and Profeta are separately entering branch labels.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The complete geography is accounted for, but no inspected source establishes one natural-river identity for the selected unnamed channels, Salar Mar Muerto interior and western model truncation. A salt-flat name or a name on a separate joining branch cannot supply that identity.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected eastern feeder runs southwest to the separately labeled Chimborazo joining setting, turns west and northwest through a converging network, crosses Salar Mar Muerto northward, and continues west past the separately entering Profeta approach. It stops inland on a mapped channel before the next western confluence.
records.completion_scope: All selected portions are geographically accounted for by the independently published natural-watercourse and surface originals. The initially apparent northward gap is occupied by the source-identified Salar Mar Muerto footprint, whose margins meet the mapped channel endings. The middle model generalizes converging channel strands; its geography is supported without certifying a channel along every model segment. The final tip is a selected truncation, not a source-confirmed hydrological terminus.
records.supported_name_scope: Salar Mar Muerto applies to the mapped intervening salt-flat surface only. The independently labeled Q. Chimborazo and Q. del Profeta approaches are distinguished from the selected headward route.

scope_limits: No natural-river hydronym is established for the complete selected system; no claim that it is officially unnamed is made.
The middle line is a generalized corridor selection, not a surveyed path through individual neighboring channel strands.
Salar passage is geographically identified; continuous flow, permanent water, overflow conditions and artificial conveyance remain unasserted.
The source channel continues beyond the selected inland tip; the model endorheic classification is not independently verified by the inspected cartography.
The two unavailable publications supply no new substantive evidence and do not prevent the bounded geographic conclusion.

bounded_name_observations.name: Salar Mar Muerto
bounded_name_observations.scope: Intervening mapped salt-flat surface only; no river-name transfer or permanent-water claim.

records.material_pending_reason: The selected northern opening and its eastward hook south of Tingui are not connected to the named Jacaré headward branch in the inspected cartography. The remaining Jacaré/Piauí corridor, reservoir passage and actual estuarine tip are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Rio Piauí is established for the lower river and estuary. Rio Jacaré is retained for the selected upper reach. Whole-system naming remains provisional because the selected opening is not source-established.
records.completion_scope: All36 selected parts were considered. Middle joins, impounded passage and actual estuarine terminal are source-accounted for; the chosen headward opening remains materially pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Rio Piauí is established for the lower river and estuary. Rio Jacaré is retained for the selected upper reach. Whole-system naming remains provisional because the selected opening is not source-established.

scope_limits: Material gap: the initial northern opening/connecting arm south of Tingui is not established by the inspected source drainage; an adjacent Rio Jacaré label alone does not close it.
The maps use distinct reach and tributary labels, including Jacaré and Piauí. No exact scalar-name transition or one name for every part is claimed.
The impounded corridor is established geographically; no contemporary operating state, hydraulic routing through structures or independent formal reservoir name is asserted.
The selected terminal is within the estuarine channel, upstream of the true ocean entrance shown farther south.
Historical source cartography is used at ordinary corridor scale, without exact bank, spring, island-margin or vertex matching.
The two stopped publications were not replaced through alternate routes. Their missing maps are not counted as evidence.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio Jacaré
bounded_name_observations.scope: Selected upper reach below the unresolved opening; not an alias for the whole group.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
